descriptionChirho: The masculine noun חֹרֶשׁ meaning a wood, forest, or wooded height, cognate with Assyrian ḫuršu (wooded height). Used of the forest/woodland where David hid from Saul in the Wilderness of Ziph (1 Sam 23:15-16, 18-19), the forests and thickets where people hid during the Philistine invasion (2 Chr 27:4, reading uncertain), the forested region in Isaiah's prophecy (Isa 17:9), and the towering cedar thicket in Ezekiel's allegory of Assyria (Ezek 31:3). The feminine form חֹרְשָׁה is a variant of the same noun. Multilingual evidence is uniform across all occurrences: Arabic الْغَابَةِ/غَابَةً (forest), German forest/Wald, Korean 숲 (forest), Spanish bosque (forest), Hindi वन/जंगल (forest/jungle), French forest. All prepositional variants (בַּחֹרְשָׁה 'in the forest,' וּבֶחֳרָשִׁים 'and in the forests,' וְחֹרֶשׁ 'and thicket') represent the same lexical meaning.
